Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

associate verb

spend time with, keep company with

also associate with, keep company with, mix with, hang out with, be close to, consort with

classical

Sen. Ep. 7.8: cum hīs versāre, quī tē meliōrem factūrī sunt
Cic. Cat. 1.10: nōbīscum versārī jam diūtius nōn potes

versor, versārī, versātus sum

verb, first conjugation, deponent; with cum and the ablative, or inter and the accusative

spend time with, move among, associate with

Lewis & Short: “to move about in a place, i. e. to dwell, live, remain, stay, abide, be in a place or among certain persons”, with in, inter, apud or cum.

Other words

  • ūtor, ūtī, ūsus sum — be on close terms with, associate with (a person)

    verb, third conjugation, deponent, with the ablative; with familiāriter, of friendship · also used · classical · Cic. Fam. 1.3.1: multōs annōs ūtor valdē familiāriter; Cic. Att. 16.5.3: Luccejus, quī multum ūtitur Brūtō (Lewis & Short)

    Lewis & Short: “to enjoy the friendship of any one; to be familiar or intimate with, to associate with a person”.

Examples

  • Cum hīs versāre, quī tē meliōrem factūrī sunt. Illōs admitte, quōs tū potes facere meliōrēs. Mūtuō ista fīunt, et hominēs, dum docent, discunt.

    Spend your time with those who will make you better; let in those whom you can make better. It works both ways: people learn while they teach.Sen. Ep. 7.8

  • A. Trebōniō, quī in tuā prōvinciā magna negōtia et ampla et expedīta habet, multōs annōs ūtor valdē familiāriter

    Aulus Trebonius, who has large and well-run business interests in your province, has been a close friend of mine for many yearsCic. Fam. 1.3.1

See also friend, associate, member, social.
